modules.name: Tool inventory and interface audit
modules.design_question: What does each existing tool read, write, store, test and depend on today, and where do the tools already agree?
modules.method: Read-only audit of the four local repos at their single commits (Vista 2 Oct, the others 20 Oct 2026). For each tool: entry files, import and export code, storage keys, vendored libraries (version strings, SHA-256), data folders with byte sizes, test files, licence files. The two classmate tools were read only through their public GitHub pages, so their rows are lower confidence. Node is not installed here, so no test was run; test counts are static. Cross-checks: the City parcel and view-cone APIs were queried live and compared with copies stored in Vista and Form Studio; local-frame constants were recomputed against the WGS 84 ellipsoid (M03). Result: no tool reads another tool's file today (no cross-references in any repo); the only shared contract is PVV's floor list; three tools carry copies of the same City and OSM data.
inputs: Vista: .3dm (render meshes only, up to 80 MB and 2,000,000 triangles, unit-scaled) or .obj; study JSON vancouver-site-study/1 (up to 1 MB, state restored from resume_hash); City addresses; BC geocoder text.
Form Studio: design JSON mountain-studio/1 (up to 1 MB: state, summary, checks); City parcel point query; four preset real sites; OSM raster tiles. No model import.
PVV: floor list JSON or CSV (up to 400 floors, area_m2 up to 100,000, height_m up to 30, shares of 112 programme ids); project JSON; brief id; typed settings.
Toolbench: none. One static page with a hard-coded TOOLS array (five tools, line 691) and a mailto feedback form.
Downtown Massing Tool (Sinnie Choi, xubynii/dtmass): parcel pick, brief, optional .3dm massing; internal project {schema, site, blocks, ramps} in local metres (page summaries, unverified).
Solar Shading Explorer (Willem Girard): NRC weather files, typology or blank block, floorplate, storeys, glazing, date and sky (README summary).
outputs: Vista: PDF report (existing and proposed views per overlapping corridor), study JSON, PNG views. No .3dm out.
Form Studio: JSON {schema, units, state, summary, checks}; .3dm with 11 to 16 layers and MountainStudio_* user strings in Vista-frame metres; PNG; SVG diagrams.
PVV: verdict, per-floor value and cost, City-charge ledger, FSR check; floor-results CSV, project JSON, SVG and PNG.
Toolbench: links to tools and an emailed feedback form. No data.
Downtown Massing Tool: live rule checks with clause links, version comparison, print-to-PDF report, DXF R12 inside a .zip (architecture review).
Solar: sun position, shading and gain charts; a .3dm written by src/export/rhino.js (contents not inspected).

modules.name: Layer 0 project schema
modules.design_question: Which one JSON document lets Vista, Form Studio, PVV and the toolbench exchange site, context, massing, floors and programme mix without re-typing?
modules.method: Adopt PVV's floor record unchanged as the canonical floors array (level, elevation_m, height_m, area_m2, area_basis, mix of programme_id and share): it is already validated and tested, and its importer already reads a top-level floors array. Geometry stays optional: floors carry no plan; massing carries plan and 3D. Store the site as lon/lat (RFC 7946) and derive local metres from a declared frame (M03). Context layers are references (manifest URL, SHA-256, licence, attribution), never geometry copies. Every estimated number carries a basis (measured, derived, assumed, unknown), mirroring PVV grades and Vista height_source. Tool-native state goes under ext.<tool> so lossy round trips cannot destroy it (Vista resume_hash, Form Studio state, PVV settings). Reserve the top-level keys floors, settings and brief because PVV's importer reads them. Validate with JSON Schema 2020-12 through Ajv; version each port type by $id. Write export adapters first, import second. Offer a CityJSON 2.0.1 LoD1 exporter for outside tools; do not use CityJSON as the working format because it has no floors, programme or checks.
inputs: Vista example study media/example-study.json (25,508 B) as the first fixture.
Form Studio design JSON and .3dm; PVV project JSON and CSV template.
City parcel and view-cone records; competition brief constants (79.2 x 144.8 m site, 9.0 FSR non-residential, 244 to 305 m).
outputs: layer0.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) with one $id per port type: Frame, Site, ContextRef, Massing, Floors, Program, ViewStudy, Checks.
Three example files: Library Square site, Shangri-La replacement (from Vista's example), five-floor PVV template.
toLayer0 and fromLayer0 adapters per tool; a CityJSON LoD1 exporter.

modules.name: Shared frame, CRS and vertical datum
modules.design_question: Which coordinate frame and vertical datum should every tool share, so a point in one tool lands on the same ground in another?
modules.method: The team's local frame is x=(lon+123.1207)*111,320*cos(49.2827 deg), y=(lat-49.2827)*110,574. Vista, Form Studio (site-context.js) and PVV (basemap manifest) use it identically. 110,574 m is the length of a degree of latitude at the equator; at 49.28 deg N the WGS 84 series gives 111,215 m. N-S distances are therefore 0.58% short, E-W 0.19% short, areas 0.77% small (about 29 m at 5 km). Vista's check against eight OSM footprints (max residual 0.08 m) shows the supplied Rhino model was built with the same formula; it does not show agreement with the ground. Recommendation: master positions in lon/lat (EPSG:4326, RFC 7946); working frame EPSG:3157 (NAD83(CSRS) / UTM 10N) via proj4js with a local origin; keep a named legacy-vista-1 converter so old studies and the supplied model can be re-registered. Vertical: every document declares a datum and grade_z per site; GeoJSON altitude is an ellipsoid height, so heights stay outside coordinate arrays.
inputs: City parcel point for 350 W Georgia St (site_id 019023251): lat 49.27970996853242, lon -123.11556575905009.
Eight OSM check points in Vista data/geo.json; view-cone vertices from the City API.
Form Studio parcel polygons (4 sites) for area comparison.

parameters.name: legacy.lon_scale
parameters.relationship: 111,320*cos(49.2827 deg) = 72,617.07 m per degree. WGS 84 value at that latitude is 72,756.7 m, so E-W is 0.19% short.

parameters.name: legacy.lat_scale
parameters.relationship: 110,574 m per degree is the equatorial value. WGS 84 series 111132.95255 - 559.84957cos2p + 1.17514cos4p - 0.0023cos6p gives 111,215.2 m at 49.2827 deg N.

parameters.name: legacy.ns_error
parameters.relationship: Distance error = 0.00580 x N-S offset: 5.8 m per km, 29 m at 5 km, about 30 m at Vista's extent corners.

parameters.name: legacy.area_error
parameters.relationship: Area factor 1.00773. Library Square stored 11,823.97 m2 against about 11,916 m2 ellipsoidal; all four preset parcels are 0.77 to 0.79% small.

parameters.name: frame.horizontal

modules.name: Nodes with typed ports: minimal refactor
modules.design_question: What is the smallest change that lets each tool read and write Layer 0 through typed ports without a rewrite?
modules.method: Each tool gets one manifest (vtm-node.json: id, version, author, licence, entry URL, origin, input and output port types, transports) and two functions: read(layer0) and write() returning a patch of the subtrees it owns. A port is a JSON Pointer into Layer 0 typed by schema $id (Site, Massing, Floors, Program, Checks, ViewStudy); the host validates with Ajv before delivery. Transport 1, no code: file export and import. Transport 2: same-origin storage plus BroadcastChannel, usable among Ruijie's tools on ruijieliu6.github.io because storage keys are already namespaced. Transport 3: window.postMessage with an exact targetOrigin and an event.origin check, for classmates' origins, only after written consent. Pages already sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin * so packs load cross-origin. Order: PVV first (its importer already accepts a floors array), Form Studio, Vista, the toolbench shell, then classmate nodes. Replace PVV's window.claude calls (downloads, AI sampling) with a host-services interface.
inputs: PVV consumes Floors, Program, Site.area_m2 and a brief id. Today only through its file importer; unknown ids such as O1 are rejected.
Vista consumes Site, Massing (prism or mesh) and views.ceiling. Today by hand: .3dm and .obj are read as-is and placement is declared by the user.
Form Studio consumes Site (parcel ring or point) and brief constants, from presets, map click or City lookup.
Toolbench shell consumes node manifests; today a hard-coded TOOLS array in index.html.
DT Mass would consume Site and offer Floors; Solar would consume Floors[0], rotation and storeys. Both only with consent.
outputs: Form Studio produces Massing, Floors and Checks; its checks[] already hold id, status, clause, sourceUrl and verifiedOn.
Vista produces ViewStudy and Checks (plan overlap by view_number, study ceiling).
PVV produces Checks (verdict, FSR) and ledgers under ext.pvv.
DT Mass produces prisms (x, y, w, d, z0, floors, f2f), Floors and rule verdicts (pass, fail, review with clause).
Solar produces gain metrics and a .3dm placed in the Layer 0 frame.

modules.name: Duplicates that become shared services
modules.design_question: Which functions and data are re-implemented or copied across the tools and should become one shared service?
modules.method: Search and read across the four repos, plus file lists of the two classmate repos. For each duplicate: count copies, bytes and divergence. Divergence found: the same City view-cone dataset sits in Vista data/viewcones.json (snapshot modified 2026-09-21, two decimals) and inside Form Studio vancouver-sites.js (modified 2026-10-12, four decimals); the live record for view 10 now has object_id 1 where Vista stored 3. PVV's basemap was built by the same generator script as Vista's unified context. Rank services by copies x bytes x risk and by how little each tool must change.

2 View-cone pack: Vista data/viewcones.json (37,707 B) and 24 polygons in Form Studio's 296,947 B vancouver-sites.js; DT Mass loads its own (unverified).
3 Site service: Vista address search (City addresses export plus BC geocoder), Form Studio parcel point lookup, DT Mass parcel pick, PVV click point.
4 Building LOD1 pack: Vista 9,897 plus 51,510 buildings as float32 meshes; PVV 5,247 as int16 rings; Form Studio convex-hull copies near four sites.
5 Rhino I/O: Vista reader (8.8 KB), Form Studio writer (27 KB), DT Mass reader, Solar writer; at least four rhino3dm builds, Vista's and Form Studio's wasm about 2.6 MB each.

7 3D viewer: three.js r128 with classic OrbitControls (Form Studio) against Vista's custom WebGL2; r186 has no build/three.min.js. Decide per tool, not before 13 Nov.

modules.name: Context packs and storage budget
modules.design_question: How should Layer 0 context data be packaged so every tool loads the same bytes once and the repository stays small?
modules.method: A pack is one .bin per layer plus a JSON manifest, as PVV already does (layer table of dtype, byte_offset, count; extent; quantum; attribution; caveats), and a release manifest with SHA-256, as Vista already does. Buildings: ring, height_dm, ground_dm, height_source, osm_way in int16 at 0.25 m. PVV's file holds 5,247 buildings in 261,080 B (49.8 B each); Vista's mesh holds 9,897 in 9,722,568 B (982 B each): 19.7 times smaller, with simplification explicit (one ring per building, holes and podium steps lost). Terrain stays a triangle mesh until the terrain packet decides. Host packs in one Pages repo (site 1 GB, 100 GB per month soft). Pages answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, ETag and Accept-Ranges (checked 21 Oct 2026), so tiles can be fetched by byte range and cached by SHA-256. Keep ODbL packs in their own folder. Export CityJSON 2.0.1 for outside tools; its integer vertices with scale and translate follow the same idea.
inputs: Vista generated/*.bin: 38,683,074 B of a 51,990,003 B release.
PVV basemap: 1,037,340 B bin plus a 1,383,120 B base64 copy.
Form Studio vancouver-sites.js: 296,947 B.
outputs: pack.manifest.schema.json and a loader (fetch, verify SHA-256, cache).
A downtown buildings-lod1 pack (target under 1.5 MB).
A removal list: PVV .b64.txt, Vista demo.gif (9.2 MB) from the served tree.

modules.name: Licence and attribution decisions
modules.design_question: Which licence applies to each part of the platform, and which decisions are still open?
modules.method: Start from facts. None of the four repos has a LICENSE file for its own code (PVV's README says to be decided before release). GitHub states that without a licence no one may reproduce, distribute or derive. List every component by type (code, schema, data packs, images, icons, fonts, vendored libraries) and attach the licence found in the repo or at source. Separate folders so share-alike data cannot reach code: OSM-derived packs stay ODbL. The Open Government Licence - Vancouver text could not be read (script-rendered page, 403 on vancouver.ca); the BC licence 2.0 is a likely template but that is unverified. Choose a code licence: Apache-2.0 adds an explicit patent grant, NOTICE file and a duty to mark changes; MIT is shortest. Our recommendation is Apache-2.0 for code, CC0 or CC BY 4.0 for the schema, and a per-pack licence file for data. Record each co-author's written agreement before the first public release.
inputs: README and vendor licence files of the four repos.
Toolbench credit lines (CC BY 3.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 2.0 and 4.0 photographs).
GitHub licensing and Pages documentation.
outputs: LICENSE (code), LICENSE-DATA per pack, NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES, CONTRIBUTING.md with a contribution-licence statement, and the matrix below as docs/licences.md.

modules.name: Permission, credit and migration plan
modules.design_question: How do we integrate the classmates' tools with permission and credit, and in what order do we migrate before 13 Nov 2026?
modules.method: Treat Sinnie Choi (Downtown Massing Tool, github.com/xubynii/dtmass) and Willem Girard (Solar Shading Explorer, github.com/willemgirard03/Shading-tool-test) as independent authors. Neither repo has a LICENSE file, so we may link and credit but not copy code. The class toolkit (GenEnv/arch540-a1-toolkit, 15 student tools) tells students to edit only their own file and states no reuse terms. Send each author a one-page request: what we want (link, screenshot, read their export, embed as a node, vendor code), what we give (credit line, repo link, right to withdraw, no edits to their code), and ask for a licence on their repo. Log replies as issues and in CONTRIBUTORS.md. Credit pattern: name, tool, repo URL, licence, date of permission. Technical order: freeze Layer 0 v1 in week 1; PVV and Form Studio adapters week 2; Vista and the shell week 3; classmate nodes only with consent. Conformance tests from M02 and M03 run in CI. Generative AI may draft adapters and tests under review; it never supplies coordinates, heights or licence terms.

flags.detail: The USGS and Open Topo Data pages state no licence or citation request. The USGS page gives EGM96 heights and no accuracy figure. Confirm before shipping terrain.

flags.claim: Hub v0.5 already reads tool exports into one project file (toolbench About page).
flags.detail: No hub code, schema or exports are in the four repos, so its 89/89 checks cannot be verified. A Structure Lab station is named in a caption but no such tool was found. Reconcile with Layer 0.

flags.claim: City open data may be combined with OSM data in one published database.
flags.detail: The OGL-Vancouver text could not be read (script-rendered page; vancouver.ca returned 403) and the 2017 OSM help thread is inconclusive. Keep layers in separate files until the City answers in writing.

flags.claim: The supplied studio model and the competition base model may be redistributed in derived form.
flags.detail: Competition terms cover templates only (7.5.5, 7.5.6) and say nothing about site plans or the 3D model. Vista publishes 38.7 MB derived from the studio model whose owner and terms are unknown. Form Studio already omits the competition model.

flags.claim: Classmates are content to be linked and shown in the toolbench.
flags.detail: Credit lines exist but no consent record is in any repo. The toolbench links to class-toolkit anchors, not to the authors' own pages (xubynii.github.io/dtmass, willemgirard03.github.io/Shading-tool-test).

flags.claim: OSM's tile server can carry the platform's map traffic (Form Studio calls tile.openstreetmap.org).
flags.detail: The policy sets no numeric limit, bans bulk download and prefetching, requires visible attribution and a Referer, and may block heavy use. GitHub Pages is not mentioned. Plan a fallback map.

flags.claim: Public Views Guidelines page and clause numbers quoted in Vista.
flags.detail: The PDF and vancouver.ca pages returned HTTP 403. References come from Vista data/guideline.json and are unchecked here.

flags.claim: The team can license AI-drawn glyphs, pictograms and AI-written code as its own.
flags.detail: Canadian law on AI authorship is unsettled (CIPPIC v Sahni; the article read dates from July 2024 and the outcome was not checked). Disclose AI use in NOTICE and prefer permissive licences.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra is available to the team for adapter work.
flags.detail: Press reports a 3 Sep 2026 launch with staged access; API availability is not stated on the page read. Do not plan around it.

flags.claim: A Form Studio .3dm lands on the right ground in Vista.
flags.detail: Form Studio exports Vista-frame XY with grade z=0, but Vista's example site sits at z 40.52 m and its importer reports file coordinates as-is and leaves placement to the user. Layer 0 needs frame and grade_z on every massing.

change_log: Round 1: first pass on C05. Read all four local repos; read public pages of two classmate repos and the class toolkit; queried City APIs and GitHub Pages headers live; recomputed frame constants against WGS 84; drafted Layer 0, port map, duplicate list, pack budget, licence matrix and permission plan.
notes: Main findings: (1) no repo has a licence for its own code, so classmates' code cannot be reused without written grants; (2) the shared local frame uses the equatorial latitude scale, so distances and parcel areas are 0.6 to 0.8% short and Layer 0 should master lon/lat with EPSG:3157; (3) PVV's floor record is the best canonical floors array, but its README example ids are invalid; (4) the same City and OSM data are copied three ways, and PVV's int16 pack is about 20 times smaller per building than Vista's mesh. Cone-height validation belongs to the view-cone packet; these cases test integration only. Node was unavailable, so no tests were run.
